documentation_gaps.description: The diagnosis of type 2 diabetes is documented, but the presence of ketosis and metabolic acidosis (pH 7.30, HCO3 16, ketones positive) suggests possible diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or ketosis-prone diabetes, which requires specification of the type of diabetes and the acute metabolic complication.
documentation_gaps.why_it_matters: Coding requires specificity for diabetes with ketoacidosis or other complications. Without clarification, the encounter may be coded as uncomplicated type 2 diabetes, undercoding the severity and acuity.

risk_flags.description: The diagnosis of type 2 diabetes is asserted, but the clinical picture (ketosis, acidosis) may be more consistent with type 1 diabetes or DKA. The diagnosis is not fully supported by the evidence.

specialist_trace.rationale: The documentation must explicitly clarify whether this is diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or a hyperglycemic crisis with ketosis, and specify the exact type of diabetes (e.g., type 1, type 2 with ketosis-prone phenotype, or LADA) based on clinical correlation (e.g., C-peptide, autoantibodies, or response to therapy). Please document the acute metabolic complication as a distinct diagnosis (e.g., “DKA” or “ketosis-prone type 2 diabetes with metabolic acidosis”) and reconcile the admission diagnosis with the laboratory findings. Without this specificity, the coding cannot accurately reflect the severity and clinical complexity of the episode.
